stable_sign_check.rule: >=60% of quarters share the mean IC's sign

placebo_check_keep_rule_literal.rule: placebo mean |IC| < 50% of real mean |IC| AND same sign as real (candidate-manifest.json keep_rule)

preregistered_gate_evaluation.note_on_wording_tension: direction-review.json's prose stop_condition is OR-phrased ('stop if unstable sign, OR placebo reproduces >=50% WITH THE SAME SIGN') and, read in isolation, would not fire here because the placebo has the OPPOSITE sign from the real result, not the same sign. candidate-manifest.json's keep_rule is the more precisely operationalized AND-structured pass/fail gate ('pass' requires BOTH stable sign AND a small-and-same-signed placebo); since the placebo's magnitude is 74.9% of the real IC's magnitude (not <50%) and has the opposite sign, the keep_rule's placebo_check clause fails either way. This pilot applies the manifest's literal AND/fail_condition as the controlling gate -- the stricter of the two readings, not a relaxation -- and reports the tension rather than silently picking whichever reading passes.

decision_reason: Real standalone IC is negative (mean -0.0565, t=-1.67 on n=8 quarters, not significant at conventional 95% for df=7) and its sign is directionally consistent across 6/8 quarters (75%, clears the 60% stability bar on its own). But the placebo (filings shuffled across tickers within the same quarter) has mean IC +0.0423 -- opposite sign, and its magnitude (74.9% of the real IC's) is far too close to the real result's to call the real result clearly distinct from noise on only 8 quarters. The keep_rule's placebo condition (<50% AND same sign) fails. Per the preregistered stop rule, this pilot does not scale beyond the 400-filing-quarter sample; the 8-K risk_score feature (this construction, this prompt, this 50-ticker sample) is not advanced further without a larger sample or a materially different construction.
